question: Can the check the fuel census said was missing actually be stood up on real repositories?

finding_1_prior_verdict_was_wrong.claim: CHECK_NO_TEST_MODULE was at least partly a finder bug, not a real absence

evidence.old_finder: globbed only test_*.py; the importing files are conftest.py and test_*.py under tests/api/

finding_1_prior_verdict_was_wrong.general_rule_violated: A finder that searches one filename convention reports a missing check, and 'no check exists' is indistinguishable from 'I did not look here'.

finding_2_finder_bugs_found_and_fixed.fix: also *_test.py, conftest.py, and every .py under test/ or tests/

finding_2_finder_bugs_found_and_fixed.bug: filename-based discovery misses tests named after the module

finding_2_finder_bugs_found_and_fixed.fix: resolve node.level against the importing file's package

finding_2_finder_bugs_found_and_fixed.bug: import name unrecoverable from the path
finding_2_finder_bugs_found_and_fixed.example: django-argcache src/function.py imported as argcache.function; name only in setup.py packages=[...]
finding_2_finder_bugs_found_and_fixed.fix: read packages=/package_dir= from setup.py, setup.cfg, pyproject.toml

finding_2_finder_bugs_found_and_fixed.bug: router dispatch invisible to an import graph
finding_2_finder_bugs_found_and_fixed.example: comics src/comics/accounts/views.py imported only by urls.py, exercised by client.get('/me/secret-key/')
finding_2_finder_bugs_found_and_fixed.fix: walk urls.py route registrations and match routes/names in tests

finding_3_census.interpretation: Even with four naming conventions, six repos, and three graph kinds, only a third of changed non-test files have any check reachable. The prior round's 42/42 unverified was measured with a finder that undercounts; the corrected number is still 67% unverifiable.

finding_4_reachability_is_not_adequacy.method: mutation testing on two real projects, baseline green, then break the code

experiments.note: an existing test imports this module; nothing asserts this behaviour

experiments.mutant: secret_key POST no longer rotates the key

finding_4_reachability_is_not_adequacy.conclusion: COVERS means a test exists and names the module. It does not mean a bug in that module is caught. Mutation is the only measurement that distinguishes the two, and it costs a test run per mutant.

finding_5_runnability.measured: stem: python -m unittest test.unit.util.connection -> OK, 28 tests, no install needed
finding_5_runnability.measured_2: comics: 9 transitive dependencies missing plus Django>=6.0.6 requires Python>=3.12 while the sandbox is 3.11; after installing 12 packages the suite ran 10 passed in 5.76s
finding_5_runnability.conclusion: Running a repository's own check is possible but costs dependency resolution and a version-constrained interpreter. It is a setup problem, not a model-capability problem.

what_this_does_not_say: It does not say the 6 round-28 tasks now verify; the finder only says a check may exist.
It does not say coverage is 33% everywhere; the corpus is 6 repositories chosen because they were the failures.
It does not close claim D: reachability, adequacy, and weight-space permanence are three different bars.

finding_6_reuse_measured.environment: three-dial lock, 1000 states, repo's own shape (canonical/runtime/environment_learning_v1.py)

experiments.note: 51 states seen of 1000, goal never observed; 600 trials still found only 79 states
the repo's existing tests pass a hand-written heuristic; the aim is the caller's, not learned
drive() explores before planning every visit; the prior changed no cost
stale prior detected instead of executed

experiments.regime: stored plan executed blind on drifted world
experiments.note: the counterfactual: unvalidated reuse lands off goal

finding_6_reuse_measured.what_the_number_means: 1.08% is the cost of replaying one already-learned plan in an UNCHANGED environment. It is not learning: nothing new is acquired on the warm visit, and the 1672-interaction learning cost is paid once by whoever found the plan.
two_easy_to_miss_false_negatives: the environment supplies reset()/snapshot()/restore() -- arbitrary rollback no real computer-use surface gives you
the caller supplies is_goal() -- the terminal verifier, which is the same missing piece as the fuel census
the caller supplies the AIM heuristic, without which the 1000-state lock is not solved at all
